comparison: Perfect agreement on TPR deletion experiments (C29-C36). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes converging evidence from localization, quantitative analysis, and functional assays. Peer reviewers found the evidence 'convincing' and 'elegant' with no concerns raised.

Complete agreement on Gαi co-localization and sequence conservation (C37-C39). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites specific figure evidence, and peer reviewers accepted findings without challenge, noting the C-terminus as the molecular determinant for cortical localization.

Full agreement on GL1 deletion analysis (C40-C45). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes systematic deletion analysis showing GL1's critical role. Peer reviewers accepted that 'the position of GoLoco1 is essential for AGS3 functioning' without raising concerns.

Disagreement on GL motif swapping experiments (C47-C55). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with consistent data demonstrating GL1 position and GL3/GL4 sequence importance. However, Peer Reviewer 3 rated this UNCERTAIN, questioning why AGS1111 and AGS2222 induce similar developmental defects despite different localization patterns.

Complete agreement on AGS4444 and AGS-GL1GL2 experiments (C56-C61). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the data supports GL3/GL4 autoinhibition and GL1 position criticality. Peer reviewers found the 'elegant genetic approaches' convincing without raising concerns.

Full agreement on AGS ortholog and chimera experiments (C62-C68). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes that functional outcomes correlate with C-terminal donor species. Peer reviewers accepted that chimeric analyses 'corroborate the notion that the GoLoco1 position is crucial.'

Agreement on AGS-PmGL cortical localization findings (C72-C73). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the experimental data from multiple figures. Peer reviewers accepted this 'unexpected' finding without dispute, though OpenEval also evaluated C75-C78 which peer reviewers grouped differently.

Partial overlap on linker region findings. OpenEval R7 addresses C72-C73, C75-C78 (SUPPORTED), while Peer R13 addresses C75-C82 (SUPPORTED). Both find the linker region evidence supported, though OpenEval separates phosphorylation findings (C79-C82) into a different result (R8).

Agreement on phosphorylation and specific amino acid findings (C79-C82). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes that specific amino acids rather than phosphorylation are important. Peer reviewers accepted these supplementary findings without challenge.

Disagreement on recruitment model evidence (C85-C92). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with convergence of localization, interaction, and functional data. However, Peer Reviewer 3 rated this UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning NuMA expression patterns shown in Figure 7, noting it appears expressed only in a subset of cells rather than ubiquitously.

Complete agreement on endomesoderm specification findings (C93-C95). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes specific reduction in marker expression territories. Peer reviewers found the evidence 'convincing' regarding asymmetric cell division and fate decisions.

Full agreement on Insc and Dlg localization findings (C96-C97). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the contrast with variable AGS localization. Peer reviewers accepted these findings without question.

Complete agreement on cross-species AGS ortholog experiments (C98-C102). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes SpAGS's unique effects in pencil urchin embryos. Peer reviewers praised the 'impressive combination of phylogenetics and molecular experiments.'

Agreement on GL1 conservation and position-specific requirements (C103-C106). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C105 involves evolutionary speculation extending beyond direct evidence. Peer reviewers accepted that 'much of the difference in ACD and micromere formation can be attributed to differences in the AGS C-terminus, in particular GL1.'
